questions.question: Which of the following ligaments extends from the cervix and vagina to the lateral pelvic wall?

suspectLines.text: The cardinal ligament (transverse cervical ligament or ligament of Mackenrodt) extends from the side of the cervix and lateral fornix of the vagina to the pelvic wall. Other ligaments of the uterus: + Broad ligament - peritoneal fold covering the ovaries and fallopian tubes. It has three parts named after the structures it covers, i.e., mesosalpinx, mesovarium, and mesometrium (largest part). + Pubocervical ligament - attaches the anterior aspect of the cervix and upper vagina to the posterior aspect of the pubic bones. + Round ligaments - arises from the lateral cornua of the uterus, passes through the inguinal canal, and attaches to the labia majora. @ + Uterosacral ligaments - passes from the back of the uterus and cervix to thegintérior surface of the sacrum.
